content_voiceover: The Hans algorithm is the immunohistochemistry surrogate used to classify diffuse large B cell lymphoma into germinal center B cell, or G-C-B, versus non-germinal center subtypes, approximating the more expensive gene expression profiling. It is a sequential three stain algorithm: first stain for C-D-ten; if positive, the tumor is classified G-C-B. If C-D-ten is negative, stain for B-C-L-six; if B-C-L-six is also negative, the tumor is non-G-C. If B-C-L-six is positive, stain for M-U-M-one; M-U-M-one positive calls it non-G-C, while M-U-M-one negative calls it G-C-B. In the original validation cohort, non-G-C-B patients had significantly worse overall survival than G-C-B patients, with a highly significant p value. On the molecular side, gene expression profiling separates D-L-B-C-L not otherwise specified into G-C-B, activated B cell or A-B-C, an unclassified group, and primary mediastinal B cell lymphoma, and more recent genomic classification schemes further subdivide these into subtypes like E-Z-B, B-N-two, M-C-D, and N-one, each with characteristic mutations, for example M-Y-D-eighty-eight L-two-six-five-P and C-D-seventy-nine A or B alterations in M-C-D, that point toward rational targeted therapies such as B-C-R pathway or B-C-L-two inhibitors.
keypoints: Hans algorithm: CD10 positive = GCB; CD10 negative + BCL6 negative = non-GCB
CD10 negative + BCL6 positive: MUM1 positive = non-GCB, MUM1 negative = GCB
Non-GCB has significantly worse overall survival than GCB (P<.001)
Gene expression profiling splits DLBCL into GCB, ABC, unclassified, and PMBL
Genetic subtypes (EZB, BN2, MCD, N1) carry distinct mutations and suggest targeted agents
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, memorize the Hans algorithm sequence: C-D-ten first, then B-C-L-six, then M-U-M-one if needed, sorting tumors into G-C-B or non-G-C-B. Non-G-C-B carries a worse prognosis. Beyond immunohistochemistry, know that gene expression profiling defines G-C-B, A-B-C, and primary mediastinal subtypes, and that newer genomic classifiers like E-Z-B and M-C-D refine this further and can point toward specific targeted agents.
